(P/anticipatory-application) This review's 139-study aggregate confirms non-HMD, monitor-based collaboration (78.4%) as the field's actual practice, contextualizing Part III's own desktop-3D-vs-video-only strata: the 'lab=VR' pole is the minority condition in the wider VRCL literature, not the default.

(P/anticipatory-application) vle-01's F7 finding ('Presence & the WE': F1-PRESENCE 4.3 vs 1.2 per-100, APP vs VID; optative co-watching language) is a stronger empirical hit for the general presence/co-viewing theme than for any construct this review develops in depth; the two should be read as parallel observations, not source-and-application, since this review never operationalizes social presence itself.

(P/anticipatory-application) The 78.4%-non-HMD / 7.2%-HMD field distribution supplies Part III a citable baseline for how atypical fully immersive HMD deployment is relative to the broader VRCL literature, useful when contextualizing the dissertation's own lab=VR / deployment=2D-PC poles.

(P/anticipatory-application) The review's own conditional non-verdict on HMD-vs-non-HMD ('depends on goals, setting, and which affordance matters most') cautions Part III against reading its VR/2D comparison as revealing context-free medium properties rather than properties contingent on collaboration design, task, and goals.

target: more immersion -> more learning <-> immersion adds presence but not learning
note: (P/anticipatory-application) This review's own staging of Makransky & Lilleholt's HMD-arousal-advantage finding against Makransky et al./Parong & Mayer's HMD-distraction finding directly instantiates this cluster's debate axis 1, without adjudicating a winner.

This unit's own qualification, stated for the compiled index's benefit: social presence is present in the VRCL literature only as a cited, undeveloped factor, never as this review's own operationalized construct — it should not be over-read as a CMC-to-VR bridge (FE).
